target: the matrix-M factorisation of the Hecke character chi^lambda at the substrate anchor -- computing chi^lambda(beta_atom; q_0) block-by-block over the per-nucleon H_3 factors instead of over the full dim V_lambda representation
target_value: chi^lambda(q_0) = sum over mu_p blocks of the matrix-M product, agreeing with the whole-representation Geck-Pfeiffer character to absolute 1e-45, and with its own two-level (mu_p, mu_n) refinement to absolute 1e-40, on all 18 tested partitions of 2H/3H/3He/4He
description:
Derivation chain for the two mpfr matrix-M witnesses -- derived-chi-catalogue-matrix-m-mpfr.witness.json (one-level mu_p) and derived-chi-catalogue-matrix-m-mu-n-mpfr.witness.json (two-level mu_p, mu_n). One producer, two levels of the same factorisation, so one chain drains both.

This is a chain about a REARRANGEMENT, not a new quantity: the character being computed is the same one either way, and the whole content is that the block-structured route reproduces it. That is why the target is stated as an agreement rather than as a number.

Trust profile: two AXIOM entrypoints (Hecke energy, Schur-Weyl/Wedderburn), two DERIVED steps (the LR branching that defines the blocks, and the q-Young resolution of identity that refines them), one SCRIPT_CITED frontier (the numerical agreement itself). No COMPUTATIONAL leaf: nothing here evaluates to a single scalar -- the witnesses record pass counts and dimension bounds.

Both witnesses are PROTON-pinned (Q_50_DIGIT_STR), which is the 2026-08-07 default for compute. The mu-n witness declared q0Anchor=muon until 2026-08-23 while computing at the proton pin; re-running the producer moved exactly two fields, q0Anchor and q0Value, and zero mathematical fields. See bean qou-ca7s.

steps.name: Hecke relation and the balanced q-integer
steps.operation: The Iwahori-Hecke algebra H_n(q) is the braid-group algebra of B_n modulo (sigma_i - q)(sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0. The eigenvalue separation (q - q^{-1}) is the per-crossing Hecke energy scale -- the AXIOM entrypoint every character in this corpus is built over.

steps.name: Wedderburn decomposition and the irreducible characters
steps.operation: At generic q, H_n(q) is split semisimple with blocks indexed by partitions lambda |- n, and chi^lambda is the character of the block V_lambda. This is what makes 'the character of a braid word' well-defined at all, and it is the second AXIOM entrypoint.
steps.output_value: H_n(q) = direct sum over lambda |- n of End(V_lambda); chi^lambda = tr on V_lambda

steps.name: Littlewood-Richardson branching H_{3A} down to H_3^{x A} -- the mu_p blocks
steps.operation: Restrict V_lambda along the subalgebra H_3(q)^{otimes A} generated by the A per-nucleon 3-strand groups. V_lambda decomposes into (mu_p)-isotypic blocks with LR multiplicities, and the character of any word supported on those groups is the sum over blocks of a product of small matrices -- the 'matrix M'. The cost is then bounded by the BLOCK sizes, not by dim V_lambda.
steps.output_value: chi^lambda(w) = sum over mu_p of tr(M_{mu_p}(w)), with max block size 9 across the tested set
steps.notes: The measured max_mu_p_block_size is 9 over 2H/3H/3He/4He, against dim V_lambda reaching 462 at 4He on the Hoefsmit path -- that gap is the whole point of the factorisation. Roadmap: docs/audits/2026-06-07-derived-chi-catalogue-tier-1-lr-factorisation.md.

steps.name: q-Young symmetrizers as a resolution of identity within each block
steps.operation: Insert sum over mu_n |- 3 of the q-Young symmetrizers e_{mu_n} inside each mu_p block. Because they sum to the identity on the block, the two-level (mu_p, mu_n) character equals the one-level mu_p character identically -- the refinement adds structure, not a new value. What it buys is that the per-(mu_p, mu_n) image dimensions are bounded by c_LR * dim mu_p * dim mu_n INDEPENDENT of dim V_lambda, which is the structural fact that makes A = 8 and A = 9 tractable.
steps.output_value: sum over mu_n of e_{mu_n} = I on every mu_p block; max (mu_p, mu_n) sub-block dim 7
steps.notes: Completeness is checked numerically as a residual, not assumed: the producer records completeness_resid per case and the witness asserts n_completeness_ok = 18 of 18. A resolution of identity that is only asserted is the kind of step that hides an error in the symmetrizer normalisation.

steps.name: mpfr evaluation at the substrate anchor, cross-checked against the Rust character
steps.operation: Evaluate both levels with mpmath.mpf at dps = 50 -- controlled precision, explicitly NOT f64 -- at the proton pin Q_50_DIGIT_STR, and compare against the independent Rust chi_q_via_gp character summed at q_0. Agreement is absolute, not relative: cumulative round-off in the matrix product is bounded by O(word_length * block_size * 10^-dps), which dominates an absolute bound for characters of O(1) magnitude at the substrate q_0.
steps.output_value: 18 of 18 partitions agree: matrix-M vs Rust to abs 1e-45; two-level vs one-level to abs 1e-40
steps.notes:
script: computations/derived_chi_catalogue_matrix_m_mpfr.py -- the frontier step, and the only one whose claim rests on a run rather than an argument.

TWO SCOPE LIMITS, both worth stating rather than leaving to be discovered.

First, the cross-check is against chi_q_via_gp, the sign-only / Geck-Pfeiffer backend (canonical per bean b0vf). It is NOT a check against the averaged, colour-weighted convention, which on lambda = (n) differs by a factor of ~7 on the individual character. So this validates the FACTORISATION against a same-convention reference; it says nothing about which convention the downstream mass channel should consume.

Second, sp.Rational was tried first (PR #1985/#1987) and lost to Rust on high-dim lambda despite the block bound: unbounded denominators grow with every multiply, so block-bounded is not arithmetic-bounded. mpmath.mpf truncates to the precision dial and costs ~constant per multiply. The speedup recorded per isotope in the witness is therefore a property of the ARITHMETIC choice, not of the factorisation, and quoting it as evidence for the factorisation would be a category error.
